ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T1_WORD_CLASSES_COMPOUN.C.mastery: Recognises a compound noun (toothbrush, post office, mother-in-law), writes its plural by changing the main word (post offices, mothers-in-law, toothbrushes), and does not write the plural on the last part only (mother-in-laws), in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T2_WORD_CLASSES_COLLECT.C.mastery: Picks the collective noun that fits a group (a pride of lions, a fleet of ships, a school of fish, a troop of monkeys, a crew of sailors) and writes it as one singular word (a flock, not a flocks) before of, and does not use one group word for every group, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.WRITIN.T2_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.P.mastery: Puts commas between the items of a list and after an opening word, writes the apostrophe for belonging (the boy's book, the boys' books) and for a short form (it's, don't) but not for a plain plural, and writes capital letters for names, the first word and I, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T3_WORD_CLASSES_PRIMARY.A.mastery: Chooses the right form of be (is, are, was, were), do (do, does, did) and have (has, have, had) as a helping verb, makes it agree with the subject, and does not write she have finished or they was playing, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.READIN.T3_INTENSIVE_READING_PO.P.mastery: Names the stanza (a group of lines), the line, the rhyme (matching end sounds), the rhythm (the beat) and the repetition (a word or line said again), and says the speaker of the poem is the persona, not always the poet, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T4_VERBS_AND_TENSE.PRESEN.mastery: Writes the simple present for habits and facts with -s after he, she or it, writes the simple past (regular -ed and irregular went, saw, ate), and uses did not with the plain verb, not did not went, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T5_WORD_CLASSES_ADJECTI.G.mastery: Uses very, quite and extremely with gradable adjectives (very tall, quite cold), uses absolutely and completely with non-gradable adjectives (absolutely perfect, completely empty), and does not write very perfect, more unique or very dead, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T6_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS.F.mastery: Uses always, usually, often, sometimes and never for how often, and very, quite, too, almost and extremely for how much, puts a frequency adverb before the main verb and after be (she always arrives, he is never late), and does not write too for very, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.WRITIN.T6_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING.S.mastery: Spells words such as separate, definitely, necessary, occasion, accommodate and tomorrow correctly, writes i before e except after c (believe, receive, ceiling) and knows the common exceptions (seize, weird), in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T7_WORD_CLASSES_PRONOUN.I.mastery: Uses someone, anybody, everything and nothing for people and things not named, writes the reflexive pronouns myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves and themselves, and does not write hisself or theirselves, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T8_WORD_CLASSES_SIMPLE_.P.mastery: Chooses at, on or in for a time or a place (at 6 o'clock, on Monday, in June, at the gate, in the room) and under, above, beside, between, opposite, behind and in front of for position, and does not write at Monday or in the morning of Friday, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T9_WORD_CLASSES_CONJUNC.C.mastery: Chooses the conjunction for a reason (because), a contrast (although), a condition (unless), a limit in time (until), two things at once (while) and a result (so), and does not write although and but together or because and so together, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.READIN.T9_INTENSIVE_READING_SI.S.mastery: Says a simile compares two things with like or as (as brave as a lion) and a metaphor says one thing is another (he is a lion), explains what the comparison means, and does not call every comparison a simile, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T10_WORD_CLASSES_DEMONST..mastery: Uses this and these for near things and that and those for far ones, matches this and that with one thing and these and those with many, and uses some, any, many, much, few and little with the right kind of noun, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T11_WORD_CLASSES_ADVERBS..mastery: Adds -ly to most adjectives (quick, quickly), changes y to i before -ly (happy, happily), changes -le to -ly (gentle, gently), writes truly, and knows that the adverb of good is well and that fast and hard stay the same, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.WRITIN.T11_MECHANICS_OF_WRITING..mastery: Adds un-, dis-, re- and mis- to the front of a word (unhappy, disagree, replay, misunderstand) and -ful, -less, -ment and -ness to the end (careful, careless, enjoyment, kindness), says how the meaning changes, and keeps the spelling right (happy, happiness), in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T12_PHRASAL_VERBS.PHRASAL.mastery: Gives the meaning of look after, look for, give up, turn off, put off, run out of, set off, break down and carry on from the sentence, and picks the right particle, not one that changes the meaning, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T13_WORD_CLASSES_COMPOUN..mastery: Joins two complete sentences with for, and, nor, but, or, yet or so and puts a comma before the conjunction, and does not join them with only a comma (a comma splice) or with no conjunction at all, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.READIN.T13_SHORT_STORY_STYLE_CL..mastery: Says that personification gives a human action or feeling to a thing or an animal (the wind whispered, the sun smiled) and that a flashback takes the story back to an earlier time, and does not call a plain description personification, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.LISTEN.T14_PRONUNCIATION_AND_IN..mastery: Names the silent letter in words such as knife (k), write (w), island (s), castle (t), honest (h), listen (t) and lamb (b), and does not pick a sounded letter, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T14_SENTENCES_ACTIVE_AND..mastery: Tells a sentence in which the subject does the action (the dog bit the boy) from one in which the subject receives it (the boy was bitten by the dog), forms the passive with be and the past participle, and does not write was bite or the boy bitten by, in 8 of 10 new items.

ENGL.G8.GRAMMA.T15_TYPES_OF_SENTENCES_I..mastery: Forms a question tag from the sentence (you are coming, aren't you; she doesn't like tea, does she), turns a positive sentence to a negative tag and a negative one to a positive tag, and does not use isn't it for every tag, in 8 of 10 new items.
